title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Likely a refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) rich in tungsten (W), possibly combined with copper (Cu).
recollection.intervention: Guess: Fabrication of a bi-continuous composite structure, possibly via co-sintering, infiltration, or additive manufacturing.
recollection.structure: Guess: Bi-continuous phase structure with interpenetrating networks of W-rich HEA and Cu.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The bi-continuous structure aims to combine high strength and thermal stability (from HEA) with high thermal conductivity (from Cu), possibly for improved performance in nuclear coolant systems.
recollection.results: Guess: Main quantitative results likely include measurements of thermal conductivity, mechanical strength, and radiation resistance, showing superior performance compared to conventional materials.

score.note: The recollection does not identify liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h and instead speculates about unrelated fabrication routes. The bicontinuous interpenetrating RHEA/Cu structure is stated only generically and is already apparent from the title, with no directional alignment, phase fractions, or W-rich interlayer. The mechanism is a generic property-combination argument rather than the selective Ti–Cu exchange, W-rich passivation, thermal transport, or irradiation-defect mechanisms reported. No quantitative results are recalled.
